title: Test speed: add a spatial index to the test oracle in rotary_field_parity

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
`app heavy: rotary_field_parity` took 417 s in the release gate (`8643d9bb7`).
It is the third longest step of the release gate.

Per-test release timings of `crates/app/tests/rotary_field_parity.rs` (wall 458.5 s on 6 workers, sum 993.1 s):
- `the_contour_kind_reads_the_radial_law`: 458.47 s
- `the_parallel_kind_reads_the_radial_law`: 264.69 s
- `the_offset_kind_reads_the_radial_law`: 243.32 s
- `the_contour_kinds_eye_cost_is_measured`: 13.15 s
- `the_offset_kinds_eye_cost_is_measured`: 9.39 s
- `the_parallel_kinds_eye_cost_is_measured`: 4.12 s

The three `eye_cost` tests run the full rotary stock simulation in 4-13 s each.
The test-only oracle `law_cut` (lines 84-105) causes almost all of the 243-458 s runtime in the three `parity` tests.
`law_cut` scans every sample in `centers(&moves)` (`H = 0.01` mm) linearly for every march step and every 3D sign probe.
`law_floor` runs up to five times per cut column to test flank steepness (lines 212-228).

What to do:
1. Add a 3D spatial grid index over `centers(&moves)` inside `crates/app/tests/rotary_field_parity.rs`.
2. Bucket each sample by its ball-and-flute bounding box with reach radius `FLUTE + R`.
3. Add a fast debug test that verifies the indexed `law_cut` matches the linear scan on sampled probes.
4. Do not change product code in `crates/sim` or `crates/app/src`.
5. Keep all nine existing tests, tolerances, and assertions unchanged.

Done means:
- All six heavy tests and all debug tests in `crates/app/tests/rotary_field_parity.rs` pass with unchanged tolerances and assertions.
- `app heavy: rotary_field_parity` release wall time drops below 60 s.
- The PR records before and after timings.

Part of #2556
